| 18 h | 0.7277 | 10× | 0.0769 (mean of 3) | 0.769 | +5.7% |

**Interpretation:**
- The back-calculated values agree with the undiluted readings within ~3–6% across the entire range — consistent with ordinary pipetting/read noise, with no systematic trend (deviations scatter in both directions).
- Critically, if the plateau (~0.7) were caused by reader saturation, a 10× dilution would land back in the linear range and the back-calculated value would be **substantially higher** than the undiluted reading. Instead, 18 h back-calculates to 0.769 — only marginally above 0.728 and well within replicate variability (replicate spread ±0.0006, dilution error ~1–2%).
- The linearity check at 5 h (2× dilution, OD ~0.35) also confirms proportional response in the linear range, anchoring the dilution math.
- The growth curve itself (exponential phase 0–6 h with doubling time ~50 min, then a stable plateau with small fluctuations around 0.70–0.76) is a classic entry into stationary phase — a biologically ordinary explanation requiring no instrumental artifact.

Conclusion: the undiluted readings faithfully represent the culture's biomass; there is no evidence of hidden biomass above the readings.
